summary_html: A **parent/guardian/child requests help** without a substantiated allegation. FFPSA created a federal pathway for **prevention services** to avert removal and stabilize families before a case escalates.
authority_html: - **Family First Prevention Services Act (2018)** — prevention services, kinship support; shifts upstream from removal to support

primary_citations.citation_text: California - Penal Code §§ 11164–11174.3 (CANRA – Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act)
California - Welfare & Institutions Code § 300 et seq. (Juvenile dependency proceedings)

regulations_applicable.title: Title 22 - Social Security (DSS Child Welfare Regulations)
Title 11 - Law (DOJ Child Abuse Central Index)

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court held that the probate court applied an incorrect legal framework in denying special immigrant juvenile predicate findings, and that a young person's uncontradicted declaration can alone support findings of parental abuse, neglect or abandonment and that return to the home country is not in the child's best interest.
key_cases.relevance: Addresses a child- or caregiver-initiated petition for protective relief made without any agency substantiation of abuse.
key_cases.quote: We conclude the probate court applied an incorrect legal framework in ruling on Saul's petition.

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
key_cases.holding: The court held that the case plan and case records provisions of the federal Child Welfare Act, 42 U.S.C. sections 671(a)(16) and 675(1), create rights enforceable by foster children under section 1983, while the guardian ad litem provision does not, and reinstated the children's substantive due process claims arising from harm suffered in state custody.
key_cases.relevance: Bears on what a caregiver or youth may demand of an agency that has assumed responsibility for a child.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that the case plan provisions of the CWA, codified at §§ 671(a)(16) and 675(1), are enforceable through § 1983.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed jurisdictional and dispositional orders entered after a mother who asked her physician for help with cocaine use was referred to the agency, holding the juvenile court did not abuse its discretion in declaring the child a dependent rather than ordering family maintenance services under section 360(b).
key_cases.relevance: Arose from a parent's own request to her doctor for help, and traces what happens when that self-referral reaches the child welfare agency.
key_cases.quote: The court has broad discretion to determine what would best serve and protect the child's interest and to fashion a dispositional order in accord with this discretion.
